Definition: {wind; by resemblance breath, i.e. a sensible (or even violent) exhalation; figuratively, life, anger, unsubstantiality; by extension, a region of the sky; by resemblance spirit, but only of a rational being (including its expression and functions)}
BiblicalUsage: Rûwach is how the Bible says wind; by resemblance breath, that is a sensible (or even violent) exhalation; figuratively, life, anger. In Daniel 2:35, we read, "…gold, broken to pieces together, and became like…"; in Daniel 4:8, "…me, whose name Belteshazzar, according to the name…". You hear it again in Daniel 4:9 — "O Belteshazzar, master of the magicians, because I…" — and in Daniel 4:18, "…king Nebuchadnezzar have seen. Now thou, O Belteshazzar…".
TheologicalSignificance: I hold rûwach close because it is part of how Scripture speaks plainly about real life. I believe rûwach is still true for us, because the God who gave it has not changed his mind.
